title: Rav Chama bar Guria
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav’s great student, noting that Rav Chama bar Guria always transmits in Rav’s name, as in [Shabbat 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.9a.4), [Shabbat 10b:3-4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.10b.3-4), 11b, [Shabbat 37a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.37a.2) and [Shabbat 139b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.139b.3); [Eruvin 9a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.9a.10), [Eruvin 46b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.46b.13), [Eruvin 47a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.47a.1) and [Eruvin 60a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.60a.16); [Megillah 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18b.11) and [Megillah 19a:19-20](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.19a.19-20); [Taanit 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.12b.8) and [Taanit 27a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.27a.7); [Moed Katan 12a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.12a.17); [Yevamot 45b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45b.14); [Gittin 86b:26-27](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.86b.26-27); [Kiddushin 76b:2-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.76b.2-3); [Bava Kamma 113b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.113b.8); [Avodah Zarah 16b:11-12](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.16b.11-12); [Menachot 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.32b.3) and [Menachot 78a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.78a.7); [Chullin 45a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45a.4); and Shabbat 9:11 [Jerusalem Talmud]. In [Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 4:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.4.15.3): a man came before Rav and told him that he was born of a gentile; Rav said, “Fit.” Rav Chama bar Guria said to him: “Wherever your feet will carry you (go quickly from here), before Shmuel comes and disqualifies you.”
Afterward he studied before Shmuel, as in [Bava Kamma 99b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.99b.8), where he raised an objection to Shmuel, and Shmuel said to him, “May your brain be muddled!”

Hyman states that all the great men of the generation received from him, among them Avin bar Huna, who transmits in Rav Chama bar Guria’s name as in [Shabbat 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66b.11-13) (the Alfasi reads “Rav Huna in the name of Rav Chama bar Guria”) and [Zevachim 62b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.62b.2);

Rabbi Chelbo transmits in Rav Chama bar Guria’s name in [Shabbat 37a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.37a.2), [Megillah 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18b.11) and [Chullin 45a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45a.4); in [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.2.4.6), the text lists Rabbi Chelbo, followed by Rav Chama bar Guria in the name of Rav Chama bar Ukva, who cites Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. Hyman proposes “Rabbi Chelbo in the name of Rav Chama bar Guria; Rav Chama bar Ukva in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina”;
Rav Chisda transmits in Rav Chama bar Guria’s name in [Menachot 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.78a.7);

Rav Minyomi bar Chilkiyah transmits in Rav Chama bar Guria’s name in [Menachot 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.32b.3). Rabbah son of Rav Huna called him “our Rabbis who are expert in the matter of halakhah” (according to one version), as in [Gittin 86b:26-27](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.86b.26-27). Rabbah bar Mechasya transmits in Rav Chama bar Guria’s name in Taanit 12a.
He is likewise mentioned in [Shabbat 82b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.82b.3) and [Pesachim 86a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.86a.9).[^3][^4]

notes.text: Saved Davidson BK99b explicitly RavChama barGuria and the imprecation לעכר מוחך, may your brain be muddled, supports finite Rav expansions and the correction of to muddle your mind. Preserve Hyman’s full Rav heading. The final Taanit יב. is 12a; the earlier list’s יב: is 12b. Preserve both different source locators.

The consulted Bava Kamma 99b directly names Rav Chama bar Guria and preserves Shmuel’s imprecation. Hyman’s always-title and leading-generation claims remain attributed, as do the Alfasi reading and Jerusalem Talmud Megillah chain repartition. The earlier Taanit 12b and final 12a remain distinct supplied locators; neither is silently normalized from the other.

The linked Bavli passages show the nested chains through Rav Chama bar Guria to Rav. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Megillah has Rav Chama bar Ukva in the chain and Hyman proposes separating it into two transmissions. Heilprin also discusses these formulations. See [Heilprin’s parallel discussion](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1353&lang=en).

The transmissions cited as Shabbat 11b can be compared with [Shabbat 11a:2-7](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.11a.2-7). The dream-fast teaching cited as Taanit 12a appears at [Taanit 12b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.12b.8), where Rabbah bar Mechasya cites Rav Chama bar Guria in Rav’s name. [Shabbat 139b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.139b.3) names Avin bar Rav Huna, whereas [Zevachim 62b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.62b.2) reads Abaye bar Huna. [Yevamot 45b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45b.14) continues at [Yevamot 46a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.46a.1). In the first version at [Gittin 86b:26-27](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.86b.26-27), Rav Chama cites Rav. The second version introduces Rav Chisda as an additional transmitter. In [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 2:4:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.2.4.6), the Hebrew places Chelbo before Guria without specifying their connection. Hyman proposes two reports. Heilprin’s parallel gives Chelbo citing Ukva in Rabbi Yose’s name. It also questions Rabbah’s name in [Eruvin 49b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.49b.4).
